claims.claim: Contact us for ur Solar Energy Solution...
claims.evidence: Only a generic message; no specific item details (panel wattage, kit components, condition, or warranty) are shown.

risks.risk: Panel wattage/efficiency is unknown; price depends heavily on whether it’s ~100W, ~200W, ~400W class, etc.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the panel’s label/sticker showing: brand, model, rated wattage (W), Voc/Isc, and serial number.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst case for an unknown used panel (assume lower wattage and no verified performance).

risks.risk: Condition/performance is unknown (possible cracks, micro-cracks, delamination, or reduced output).
risks.proof: A photo of the backsheet/edges plus a working test: IV curve or at least a multimeter reading under sunlight (or a power output test report).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed to meet rated output (assume reduced performance).

risks.risk: Whether this is only the panel or a full solar kit is unknown; seller text suggests a “solution”.
risks.proof: List of what’s included with photos: panel(s) count, inverter model, battery type/capacity, charge controller specs, cables, and mounting/rails.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a single standalone solar panel only (no inverter/battery).

risks.risk: Compatibility/connector type is unknown (MC4 vs other), affecting installation cost.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the junction box and connectors (MC4 markings) and the cable length/condition.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming standard MC4 but with no guarantee; installation may require extra parts.

proof_requests: Clear label close-up on the panel showing brand, model, rated wattage (W), Voc, Isc, and serial number.
Photo of the junction box and connectors (MC4 markings) plus cable condition.
Show what is included in the “solar energy solution” (panel count, inverter model, battery type/capacity, charge controller specs).
Any proof of performance: test report, IV curve, or a power output measurement under sunlight.
response.reason: From the photo, it’s only possible to confirm a solar panel exists; the key pricing drivers (rated wattage/model, quantity, and whether it’s a full kit) are not readable or shown. Without that, a correct worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
